Definition: to sling; also to carve (as if a circular motion, or into light forms)
BiblicalUsage: The same word slings a stone and carves a wall: David slang a stone and smote the Philistine in his forehead, seven hundred chosen men of Benjamin could sling stones at a hair's breadth and not miss, and Solomon carved the walls of the house round about with cherubims and palm trees and open flowers.
TheologicalSignificance: I find it striking that one word covers the sling and the chisel, as if Scripture is saying the same hand that fights can also beautify.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
